subject.title: fix(shared): re-throw non-ENOENT errors in ignore-rules file reading

question: Should an unreadable existing .gitignore-style file abort skill/session discovery, or should OpenClaw warn and continue without that file's rules?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible: failing prevents silently scanning content the user intended to exclude, while continuing preserves the shipped best-effort availability contract; repository policy cannot choose that product tradeoff automatically.

options.title: Fail with context
options.body: Propagate non-ENOENT failures with the ignore-file path and prove that callers present an actionable error instead of silently omitting rules.

options.title: Warn and continue
options.body: Preserve discovery availability by logging a visible warning while skipping only the unreadable ignore file.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Keep the shipped best-effort behavior until the affected skill and session owners confirm the desired failure contract.

recommendation.title: Fail with context
recommendation.body: Propagate non-ENOENT failures with the ignore-file path and prove that callers present an actionable error instead of silently omitting rules.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal spans both caller surfaces whose behavior changes under this PR.
